log: The barbarians as a civilization any ruleset can give its raiders (civ-clone/web-renderer#169): `Barbarian`, its leader `Attila`, its attributes (people, nation, colours) and `isBarbarian(player)`.

Importing the package registers the attributes only. The civilization and leader are deliberately kept out of the `CivilizationRegistry` and `LeaderRegistry`, so they are never offered as a choice, drawn for a player added mid-game or brought back for a destroyed civilization; a ruleset registers them just before it claims them for the barbarian player.
Civ1's barbarians (civ-clone/web-renderer#169), from v474.05 `GameEngine.cs` `F0_1238_0980_GenerateBarbarianUprising`:
`Spawning` rules gate every spawn; `civ1-barbarians:spawning/from-turn` opens on turn (5 − level) × 30.

`turn/start/sea-landing`: every 8th turn until anyone has Automobile, a Sail (Frigate from turn 300) with 1–3 Swordmen (Knights after Explosives) and a Diplomat, on a sea of at least 16 squares clear of the poles.

`turn/start/land-uprising`: one of 128 city slots a turn, any civilization's; a chance of its gold in 100; up to 99 tries within 6 of the city re-centred on the nearest; Horsemen and Chariots in fours (Musketmen and Cannon after Industrialization), a Diplomat last.
`city/build/raiders-only`: a barbarian city builds attacking units at least two civilizations can build.
`lib/barbarianPlayer`: made by the first spawn through `civ1-player`'s `addPlayer`, on Anarchy for good, with the starting-advances rule held off.
Found by the repository's first CI run (civ-clone/web-renderer#169). 0.1.1.
Review of civ-clone/web-renderer#169:
`city/build/raiders-only` allows land units only: a Battleship, Bomber or Nuclear scored as an attacker, and the barbarians' client moves land units and transports only.
`spawnUnits` removes a unit the ship refuses (`stow` returning false) instead of leaving it asleep at sea in no manifest; the sea-landing test now registers the capacity rules and checks the cargo.

`turnCount`: v474.05 spawns once everyone has moved in its count C, and the raiders first move in C + 1. The `Start` rules run as turn V begins, which plays count V − 1, so the count they test is V − 2. The gate, the 8th-turn check and the raider count all read it, one turn later than before.
`barbarianPlayer` joins the turn under way (the end of `currentPlayers`) when the turn has queued its players already, so the first raiders move the turn they appear.

package.json: `core-yield` and `core-unit-transport` dropped; `core-civilization`, `core-engine` and `core-government` are the tests' alone and move to devDependencies, with `core-terrain`, `core-player-world` and `base-science-advance-chivalry` they also import. Tests for the registered `Build` rule and the queue.
The repository's CI found it: civ1-player's tests/lib/Generator extends its BaseGenerator.

For civ-clone/web-renderer#169: a barbarian unit makes no `Contact` and none is made with one, and a `may-negotiate/not-the-barbarians` rule answers no whenever either player is the barbarians. A rule rather than a criterion on the existing two, because `mayNegotiate` falls back to its default spacing when no rule applies.
For civ-clone/web-renderer#169: `turn/end/conquest` counts the civilizations left and the civilizations that started, and `conquestBonusFor` the opponents, the barbarian player being none of them.
For civ-clone/web-renderer#169.
For civ-clone/web-renderer#169: the three defeat rules skip the barbarian player; `turn:start` puts the barbarians at the head of the current-player order, as v474.05's slot 0.
For civ-clone/web-renderer#169: `player/action/choose-research` is never offered to the barbarian player, and `city/captured/steal-advance` doesn't apply when either side is the barbarians.

`lib/requiredAdvances` exports the advance each unit needs; `Rules/City/build` makes its rules from it. The `requires-advance` and `obsolete` rules no longer apply to a barbarian city (civ-clone/web-renderer#169): its player has no advances, and `civ1-barbarians` says what it may build.

For civ-clone/web-renderer#169: a `StrategyAIClient` with its own registry of two strategies. `Raid` plays a unit's turn after v474.05's `MoveBarbarianUnit`: a ship sails for the city with the best gold for the distance and lands its raiders beside it on that city's continent (`barbarians:landed`); a raider marches on the nearest city of a civilization worth raiding, scoring each step as Civ1 does; the leader keeps to the stack; raiders near the poles leave and stranded ones give up every fourth turn. `BuildRaiders` builds the strongest attacker the `Build` rules allow a barbarian city, else the strongest defender. Registered in the AI client registry.
Review of civ-clone/web-renderer#169:

`Disembark` leaves a stowed unit's `Stowed` busy state, and a busy unit is never active again, so raiders landed from a ship never moved: each is `activate()`d before it disembarks. Landing is also tried after sailing, not only before.

A ship whose best target was inland, or lay beside it with nowhere to land, floated for ever: it now sails for the best-scoring city it can reach a sea square beside (its own square excluded), and is removed when there is none.

A raider that captures a city stops and holds it, as one in its own city does; the leader stops on his friend's square instead of stepping off again; an enemy city next door is always entered, defended or not; only a plain `Move` counts as a step (an `Embark` extends `Move` and put raiders back aboard).
Scoring as v474.05: +4 onto any square but the unit's own city, +2 per axis that agrees with the way to the target (straight on +4).
`BuildRaiders` builds land units only (no Battleship, Bomber or Nuclear, which `Raid` can't use), the dearest attacker first as decision 3 says. The client keeps its dependencies for `actionFailed`.
